questions.question: In wheat which root system is found
questions.explanation: Wheat is a monocot plant and has a fibrous root system.

questions.question: Find out the correct statement about fibrous root system
options: Fibrous roots develop from base of stem
questions.explanation: Both B (Fibrous roots develop from base of stem) and C (Found in monocots) are correct statements about the fibrous root system.

questions.question: Primary roots and its branches constitute:
questions.explanation: (B) Primary roots and its branches constitute tap root system. [New NCERT Class 11th Page No. 57, 58]

hi.question: प्राथमिक मूल और इसकी शाखाएं मिलकर बनाती हैं:

questions.question: Root is distinguishable from stem in
questions.explanation: Roots are distinguishable from stems by having a root cap, root hairs, and the absence of nodes and internodes.

questions.question: Root meant for
questions.explanation: Roots function in fixation of the plant, absorption of water, and storage of food, making all of the above correct.

questions.question: Given below are two statements. One is labelled as Assertion (A) and other is labelled as Reason (R): Assertion (A): In Monstera and banyan trees, roots are adventitious. Reason (R): When roots arise from other parts of the plant than radicles, they are called adventitious roots. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
Both A and R are true but R is a correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not a correct explanation of A.
questions.explanation: In Monstera and banyan trees, roots arise from parts of the plant other than the radicle, making them adventitious roots. The definition of adventitious roots, as stated in Reason (R), correctly explains why the roots in Monstera and banyan trees are categorized as such. [NCERT 11th Edition 2024-25 Page No. 56]

questions.question: The roots that originate from the base of the stem are:
questions.explanation: Fibrous roots originate from the base of the stem, replacing the primary root in monocotyledonous plants like wheat. These roots are thin, thread-like, and spread out in a cluster. Unlike the primary root system found in dicots, fibrous roots provide better anchorage and efficient absorption of nutrients in shallow soil.

hi.question: वे मूल जो तने के आधार से निकलती हैं, वे हैं:

questions.question: How many of the following plants possess tap root system?(Grass, Monstera, mustard plant, wheat plant, maize)
questions.explanation: These roots originate from the base of the stem and constitute the fibrous root system, as seen in the wheat plant. In some plants, like grass, Monstera and the banyan tree, roots arise from parts of the plant other than the radicle and are called adventitious roots. The primary roots and its branches constitute the tap root system, as seen in the mustard plant.

questions.question: Roots originating from parts other than radicle are
questions.explanation: Explanation: Adventitious roots are those that develop from parts of the plant other than the radicle, such as stems, leaves, or nodes. Examples include the roots in grass, Monstera, and banyan trees. These roots provide additional support and perform various specialized functions.

hi.question: मूलांकुर के अतिरिक्त अन्य भागों से निकलने वाली मूल हैं:

questions.question: All are the functions of root system in plants except
options: absorption of water and minerals from the soil
providing a proper anchorage to the plant parts
questions.explanation: The root system in plants primarily functions in absorption of water and minerals from the soil, providing anchorage, and synthesizing plant growth regulators. However, assimilation of food is not a function of roots; it is primarily performed by leaves through photosynthesis. [New NCERT Class 11 Page No. 56]

hi.question: पादपों में मूल तंत्र के कार्य निम्न को छोड़कर सभी हैं
options: मृदा से जल और खनिजों का अवशोषण
पादप के भागों को उचित सहारा प्रदान करना
hi.explanation: पादपों में मूल तंत्र मुख्य रूप से मृदा से जल और खनिजों के अवशोषण, सहारा प्रदान करने और पादप वृद्धि नियामकों के संश्लेषण में कार्य करता है। हालाँकि, भोजन का स्वांगीकरण जड़ों का कार्य नहीं है; यह मुख्य रूप से पत्तियों द्वारा प्रकाश संश्लेषण के माध्यम से किया जाता है। [New NCERT Class 11 Page No. 56]

questions.question: A root grows in length, which region of the root is responsible for this growth?
questions.explanation: The region of elongation is responsible for the increase in root length.

questions.question: Root hairs are present in/on:
questions.explanation: Root hairs are found in the region of maturation, where they aid in water and nutrient absorption.

questions.question: The region or part of root that increases the surface area for water absorption is
questions.explanation: Root hairs are unicellular extensions of the epidermis that greatly increase the surface area of roots. This helps in efficient absorption of water and minerals from the soil.

hi.question: जड़ का वह क्षेत्र या भाग जो जल अवशोषण के लिए सतही क्षेत्रफल को बढ़ाता है:
hi.explanation: मूल रोम बाह्यत्वचा के एककोशिकीय प्रवर्ध होते हैं, जो मूल (जड़ों) के सतही क्षेत्र को काफी बढ़ा देते हैं। यह मृदा से जल और खनिजों के कुशल अवशोषण में मदद करता है।

questions.question: Which of the following protects root tip?
questions.explanation: The root cap and thimble-like structure both protect the root tip.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct with respect to the figure given below showing different zones of a typical root?
options: Part B mainly helps in absorption of water.
The cells of A region are very small.
Cells in B region are responsible for the growth of the root in length.
Proximal to C region is called the region ofmaturation.
questions.explanation: A few millimetres above the root cap is the region of meristematic activity. The cells of this region are very small, thin-walled and with dense protoplasm. They divide repeatedly. The cells proximal to this region undergo rapid elongation and enlargement and are responsible for the growth of the root in length. Root hairs absorb water and minerals from the soil. [New NCERT Class 11th Page No. 59]

hi.question: दिए गए चित्र में एक विशिष्ट जड़ के विभिन्न क्षेत्रों को दर्शाते हुए, निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा कथन सही है?
options: भाग B मुख्य रूप से पानी के अवशोषण में मदद करता है।
A क्षेत्र की कोशिकाएँ बहुत छोटी होती हैं।
B क्षेत्र की कोशिकाएँ जड़ की लंबाई में वृद्धि के लिए जिम्मेदार होती हैं।
C क्षेत्र के समीपस्थ भाग को परिपक्वता क्षेत्र कहा जाता है।
hi.explanation: मूल गोप के कुछ मिलीमीटर ऊपर विभज्योतक क्रिया का क्षेत्र होता है। इस क्षेत्र की कोशिकाएँ बहुत छोटी, पतली भित्तियों वाली और घने प्रोटोप्लाज्म वाली होती हैं। वे बार-बार विभाजित होती हैं। इस क्षेत्र के समीपस्थ कोशिकाएँ तेजी से लम्बी और बड़ी होती हैं और जड़ की लंबाई में वृद्धि के लिए जिम्मेदार होती हैं। मूल रोम मृदा से पानी और खनिज अवशोषित करते हैं।

questions.question: Adventitious roots of............. get swollen and store food.
questions.explanation: Sweet potato has adventitious roots modified for food storage.

questions.question: Supporting roots coming out of the lower nodes of the sugarcane stem are called
questions.explanation: In sugarcane, supporting roots arising from lower nodes are called stilt roots.

questions.question: In Rhizophora, roots are modified to form
questions.explanation: In Rhizophora, roots are modified into pneumatophores for respiration in waterlogged conditions.

questions.question: The hanging structures that support banyan tree are called
questions.explanation: In the banyan tree, hanging roots that provide support are called prop roots.

questions.question: Which of the following plant have stilt root?
questions.explanation: Sugarcane has stilt roots, which arise from lower nodes to provide mechanical support.

questions.question: Which of the following is incorrect about {A}, {B}, {C} and D
options: Tap roots of carrot, turnip and adventitious root of sweet potato, get swollen and store food
Pneumatophores help to get oxygen for respiration
Pneumatophore is found in the plants that grow in sandy soil.
{A}, {B} and {C} are underground roots but {D} grows vertically upwards
questions.explanation: Pneumatophores are found in plants growing in swampy or waterlogged conditions, not in sandy soil.

questions.question: In which plants the leaf base is swollen?
questions.explanation: In leguminous plants, the leaf base is swollen and is known as the pulvinus. This structure allows movement of the leaf, as seen in plants like Mimosa pudica (touch-me-not plant).

hi.question: किन पादपों में पर्णाधार फूला हुआ होता है?
hi.explanation: फलीदार पादपों में पर्णाधार फूला हुआ होता है, जिसे पर्णवृंततल्प कहा जाता है। यह संरचना पत्ती की गति में सहायता करती है, जैसा कि मिमोसा पुदिका (छुईमुई) पादप में देखा जाता है।

questions.question: Fill in the blank. Leaves originate from.............. and are arranged in an.............. order
questions.explanation: Leaves originate from the shoot apical meristem and are arranged in an acropetal order, meaning the younger leaves are towards the apex and older leaves are at the base.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a part of a leaf?
questions.explanation: Pedicel is the stalk of a flower, not a part of a leaf. A typical leaf consists of: Leaf base Petiole Lamina (leaf blade)

hi.question: निम्न में से कौन सा पत्ती का भाग नहीं है?

questions.question: Leaf base may bear two lateral small leaf like structures called:
questions.explanation: Stipules are small, leaf-like structures found at the base of the leaf in some plants

questions.question: Swollen leaf base found in some leguminous plants is called:
questions.explanation: (D) In some leguminous plants the leafbase may become swollen, which is called the pulvinus. [New NCERT Class 12 Page No. 60]

questions.question: Presence of sheathing leafbase covering the stem partially or wholly is the characteristic of certain -
questions.explanation: In monocots, the leaf base is often sheathing, partially or wholly covering the stem, as seen in grasses, bananas, and other monocots.

questions.question: What is the function of thin flexible petiole?
options: It helps the plant to climb
It increases the rate of respiration
It allows leaf blade/lamina to flutter in wind there by cooling the leaf and bringing fresh air to leaf surface
It decreases the rate of transpiration
questions.explanation: A thin, flexible petiole allows the lamina to flutter in the wind, which helps cool the leaf and bring fresh air to the surface, facilitating gas exchange.

questions.question: Given below is the diagram of a typical leaf. In which of the following all the four parts labelled as A, B, C and D are correctly identified? A B C D (1) Lamina Axillary bud Stipule Leaf base (2) Lamina Stipule Axillary bud Leaf base (3) Lamina Axillary bud Stipule Pedicel (4) Leaflet Axillary bud Stipule Leaf base
questions.explanation: Identification of labeled parts: A - Lamina (broad part of the leaf) B - Axillary bud (present at the axil of the leaf) C - Stipule (small lateral outgrowth at the leaf base) D - Leaf base (the basal part attaching the leaf to the stem) Thus, option (1) Lamina - Axillary bud - Stipule - Leaf base is correct.

questions.question: Read the following statements carefully.A. Leaf base may bear two lateral small leaf like structures called stipules.B. In dicots, the leaf base expands into a sheath covering the stem partially or wholly.C. Veins provide rigidity to the leaf bladeD. In monocots, leaf base is swollen and is known as pulvinus.E. The petiole holds the blade to obtain maximum light. How many statement (s) is/are incorrect?
questions.explanation: Explanation: Statement II is incorrect. In dicots, leaf bases rarely form a sheath; this is characteristic of monocots (e.g., grasses). Statement IV is incorrect as Pulvinus is a swollen structure at the petiole base in some dicots and legumes (e.g., Mimosa), not a typical monocot feature.

questions.question: Arrangement of vein, veinlets is called
questions.explanation: The arrangement of veins and veinlets in a leaf is termed venation. It plays a crucial role in the conduction of water, nutrients, and mechanical support to the leaf.

questions.question: Mark the option with incorrect pairing.A. Leaves - Originate from shoot apical meristem.B. Veins - Provide rigidity to the leaf blade.C. Pulvinus - Present in the leaves of most monocots.D. Venation - Arrangement of leaves on the stem or branch.E. Photosynthetic stem - Australian acacia
questions.explanation: In some leguminous plants the leafbase may become swollen, which is called the pulvinus. The arrangement of veins and the veinlets in the lamina of leaf is termed as venation.

questions.question: Leaf in which incision is absent or incomplete is called:
questions.explanation: A simple leaf has an undivided lamina, or if incisions are present, they do not reach the midrib. [New NCERT Class 11th Page No. 60]

hi.question: वह पत्ती जिसमें कटाव अनुपस्थित या अधूरा हो, कहलाती है:

questions.question: In a pinnately compound leaf (as seen in Neem) a number of leaflets are present on a common axis, the rachis. The rachis represents the -
questions.explanation: In a pinnately compound leaf (e.g., Neem), multiple leaflets are arranged along the rachis, which is a continuation of the midrib of the leaf.

questions.question: In silk cotton the phyllotaxy is
How many leaves are present at a node in opposite phyllotaxy?
questions.explanation: In opposite phyllotaxy, two leaves grow at a single node, positioned opposite to each other. Example: Guava (Psidium guajava).

questions.question: Study the given figures and identify the kind of phyllotaxy. (i) (ii) (iii)(1) Whorled Opposite Alternate(2) Alternate Opposite Whorled(3) Opposite Alternate Whorled(4) Opposite Whorled Alternate
questions.explanation: [New NCERT Class 11th Page No. 61]

questions.question: Which of the following shows whorled phyllotaxy?
questions.explanation: Phyllotaxy refers to the arrangement of leaves on a stem or branch. It can be alternate, opposite, or whorled. In whorled phyllotaxy, more than two leaves arise at a node forming a whorl. Alstonia exhibits this type of phyllotaxy, where leaves are arranged in a whorl at each node. [New NCERT Class 11 Page No. 61]

questions.question: Phyllotaxy is
options: Mode of leaf arrangement on stem
Arrangement of sepals and petals in a flower
questions.explanation: Phyllotaxy refers to the pattern of arrangement of leaves on the stem or branch of a plant. It is of three main types: alternate, opposite, and whorled. This arrangement is crucial for optimizing light capture for photosynthesis.

questions.question: Alternate phyllotaxy is present in
questions.explanation: Alternate phyllotaxy is a type of leaf arrangement in which a single leaf arises at each node in an alternate manner. This type is seen in plants like China rose (Hibiscus rosa-sinensis), mustard, and sunflower. In contrast, opposite phyllotaxy (where two leaves arise at a node opposite to each other) is seen in guava, and whorled phyllotaxy (where more than two leaves arise at a node) is found in Alstonia.

questions.question: What does (X) represent in the following figure?
questions.explanation: Stems could be modified for protection, photosynthesis, climbing, food storage roles. Slender and delicate stem modification i.e. tendrils aid in climbing. These are spirally coiled structures found in plants such as grapevines.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a stem modification?
questions.explanation: The pitcher of Nepenthes is not a modification of the stem; it is a modified leaf that helps in insect trapping for nutrition.

questions.question: Match Column I with Column II
questions.explanation: Matching explanation: A - IV: Bud in the axil of the leaf → Simple leaf B - III: Bud absent in axil of leaflets → Compound leaf C - II: Spines (modified leaves) → Cacti D - I: Leaves modified to catch insects → Pitcher plant and Venus Fly Trap E - V: Fleshy leaves with stored food → Garlic and Onion

questions.question: Leaves are modified into tendrils in -
questions.explanation: In Pea (Pisum sativum), leaves are modified into tendrils to help the plant climb by coiling around a support.

sections.name: Morphology of Flowering Plants : DPP of Lec 2 (Quiz)
sections.displayName: Morphology of Flowering Plants : DPP of Lec 2 (Quiz)

questions.question: Stem develops from............of the embryo of a germinating seed.
questions.explanation: The stem develops from the plumule of the embryo in a germinating seed.

hi.question: तना अंकुरशील बीज के भ्रूण के ............ से विकसित होता है।

questions.question: ...............are the regions of the stem that bear leaves.
questions.explanation: Nodes are the regions of the stem that bear leaves.

questions.question: Stems of potato, ginger and turmeric are modified to
questions.explanation: The stems of potato, ginger, and turmeric are modified to store food.

questions.question: In gourds, axillary buds develop spirally coiled structures called
questions.explanation: In gourds, axillary buds develop into spirally coiled tendrils, which help in climbing.

questions.question: What protects Bougainvillea from grazing animals
questions.explanation: Thorns protect Bougainvillea from grazing animals by acting as a mechanical defense.

questions.question: Stems are modified into flattened structures, which carry out photosynthesis in
questions.explanation: In Opuntia, stems are modified into flattened structures (phylloclades) that carry out photosynthesis in xerophytic conditions.

questions.question: Chlorophyll containing fleshy cylindrical structures found in Euphorbia are modified
questions.explanation: In Euphorbia, the stem is modified into fleshy, cylindrical structures that contain chlorophyll and perform photosynthesis.

questions.question: In Pistia and Eichhornia, stems are modified to form
questions.explanation: In Pistia and Eichhornia, stems are modified to form offsets, which help in vegetative propagation.

questions.question: Stem modified into green, flattened branches of unlimited growth for assimilatory function is
questions.explanation: A phylloclade is a stem modified into green, flattened branches with unlimited growth for photosynthesis, seen in Opuntia and Euphorbia.

questions.question: Which is not a modification of stem?
questions.explanation: The pitcher of Nepenthes is a modified leaf, not a stem modification.

questions.question: Which of the following is main function of stem
options: Spread branches bearing leaves, flowers and fruits
questions.explanation: The main function of the stem is the conduction of water and minerals through xylem and phloem.

questions.question: Which of the following is a modified stem meant for storage of food?
questions.explanation: Ginger is a modified stem (rhizome) meant for storage of food and vegetative propagation.

questions.question: The eyes of potato bear
questions.explanation: The eyes of a potato bear axillary buds, which can sprout into new shoots for vegetative propagation.

questions.question: Young stem is
questions.explanation: A young stem is green due to the presence of chlorophyll, enabling photosynthesis.

questions.question: In Bougainvillea, thorns are the modifications of
questions.explanation: In Bougainvillea, thorns are modifications of the stem. These hard, pointed structures help in protection and support.

questions.question: An example of edible underground stem is
questions.explanation: Potato is an edible underground stem, specifically a tuber. It stores starch and has "eyes" which are axillary buds for vegetative propagation.

questions.question: Function of stem is -
questions.explanation: The stem performs multiple essential functions, including: Bearing leaves and branches for photosynthesis and reproduction. Conducting water and minerals from roots to other parts. Conducting and storing food in modified stems like tubers and rhizomes. Thus, all the given functions are correct.

questions.question: Stem tendrils (climbing in function) develop from the axillary bud. Stem tendrils are in all of the following except:
questions.explanation: Citrus does not have stem tendrils. Instead, it has spines, which are modified stems for protection. Stem tendrils arise from axillary buds in climbers like cucumber, pumpkin, watermelon, and grapevines to provide mechanical support.

questions.question: Thorn of Citrus and Bougainvillea is modified
questions.explanation: In Citrus and Bougainvillea, thorns are modified stems that arise from the axillary buds. They serve a protective function by deterring herbivores from eating the plant.

questions.question: In plants like Jasmine and Mint, a slender lateral branch arises from the base of main axis and after growing aerially for some time arch downwards to touch the ground and forms new plant. Such lateral branches are called -
questions.explanation: In plants like Jasmine and Mint, a slender lateral branch arises from the base of the main axis, grows aerially, then bends downward to touch the ground and form a new plant. Such lateral branches are called Stolons.

questions.question: In which of the following plants, underground stems spread to new niches and when older parts die new plants are formed -
questions.explanation: In grasses and strawberry, underground stems spread to new niches, and as the older parts die, new plants are formed. This is an example of vegetative propagation through stolons or runners.

questions.question: Arrangement of leaves on stem is known as-
questions.explanation: The arrangement of leaves on a stem or branch is called phyllotaxy. It determines how leaves are arranged to maximize light capture for photosynthesis. The three main types are alternate, opposite, and whorled.

questions.question: Arrangement of vein, veinlets is called
questions.explanation: The arrangement of veins and veinlets in a leaf is termed venation. It plays a crucial role in the conduction of water, nutrients, and mechanical support to the leaf.

questions.question: In which plants the leaf base is swollen?
questions.explanation: In leguminous plants, the leaf base is swollen and is known as the pulvinus. This structure allows movement of the leaf, as seen in plants like Mimosa pudica (touch-me-not plant).

hi.question: किन पादपों में पर्णाधार फूला हुआ होता है?
hi.explanation: फलीदार पादपों में पर्णाधार फूला हुआ होता है, जिसे पर्णवृंततल्प कहा जाता है। यह संरचना पत्ती की गति में सहायता करती है, जैसा कि मिमोसा पुदिका (छुईमुई) पादप में देखा जाता है।

questions.question: Arrangement of leaves on stem or branch of stem is called
questions.explanation: The arrangement of leaves on a stem or branch to maximize light capture for photosynthesis is called phyllotaxy. It can be of three types: alternate, opposite, and whorled.

questions.question: Phyllode is modified
questions.explanation: A phyllode is a modified leaf or petiole that becomes flattened and takes over the function of photosynthesis, usually in plants where leaves are reduced to minimize water loss. Example: Acacia.

questions.question: How many leaves are present at a node in opposite phyllotaxy?
questions.explanation: In opposite phyllotaxy, two leaves grow at a single node, positioned opposite to each other. Example: Guava (Psidium guajava).

questions.question: Leaf pitcher is found in
options: Plants growing in nitrogen poor soil
questions.explanation: The leaf pitcher is found in: Nepenthes, an insectivorous plant. Plants growing in nitrogen-poor soil, where the pitcher helps trap insects for nitrogen. Thus, all options are correct.

questions.question: In silk cotton the phyllotaxy is
Fill in the blank. Leaves originate from.............. and are arranged in an.............. order
questions.explanation: Leaves originate from the shoot apical meristem and are arranged in an acropetal order, meaning the younger leaves are towards the apex and older leaves are at the base.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a part of a leaf?
questions.explanation: Pedicel is the stalk of a flower, not a part of a leaf. A typical leaf consists of: Leaf base Petiole Lamina (leaf blade)

hi.question: निम्न में से कौन सा पत्ती का भाग नहीं है?

questions.question: Leaf base may bear two lateral small leaf like structures called:
questions.explanation: Stipules are small, leaf-like structures found at the base of the leaf in some plants

questions.question: Swollen leaf base found in some leguminous plants is called:
questions.explanation: (D) In some leguminous plants the leafbase may become swollen, which is called the pulvinus. [New NCERT Class 12 Page No. 60]

questions.question: Which one of the following plants shows alternate phyllotaxy?
questions.explanation: In alternate phyllotaxy, a single leaf grows at each node in an alternate manner along the stem. Sunflower (Helianthus annuus) exhibits this type of leaf arrangement. Guava (B) and Calotropis (D) exhibit opposite phyllotaxy. Nerium (C) shows whorled phyllotaxy.

questions.question: Leaf in which incision is absent or incomplete is called:
questions.explanation: A simple leaf has an undivided lamina, or if incisions are present, they do not reach the midrib. [New NCERT Class 11th Page No. 60]

hi.question: वह पत्ती जिसमें कटाव अनुपस्थित या अधूरा हो, कहलाती है:

questions.question: Leaves -
options: Are arranged in an acropetal order
Are the most important vegetative organs for photosynthesis
questions.explanation: Leaves originate from the shoot apical meristem. They are arranged in an acropetal order (younger leaves at the top, older at the base). They are the primary organs for photosynthesis.

hi.question: पतियाँ:
options: प्ररोह शीर्षस्थ विभज्योतक से उत्पन्न होती हैं
अग्राभिसारी क्रम में व्यवस्थित होती हैं
प्रकाश-संश्लेषण के लिए सबसे महत्त्वपूर्ण कायिक अंग होती हैं
hi.explanation: पत्तियाँ प्ररोह शीर्षस्थ विभज्योतक से उत्पन्न होती हैं। ये अग्राभिसारी क्रम में व्यवस्थित होती हैं (ऊपरी भाग में नई पत्तियाँ तथा आधार की ओर पुरानी पत्तियाँ होती हैं)। ये प्रकाश-संश्लेषण के लिए प्रमुख अंग होती हैं। अतः सही उत्तर: D — उपर्युक्त सभी

questions.question: Which of the following is correct?
options: The leaf is a lateral, generally flattened structure on stem
A typical leaf consists of three main parts (leaf base, petiole and lamina)
Stipule is the lateral appendage of leaf base
questions.explanation: The leaf is a lateral, generally flattened structure on the stem. A typical leaf consists of three main parts: leaf base, petiole, and lamina. Stipules are lateral appendages of the leaf base.

questions.question: Presence of sheathing leafbase covering the stem partially or wholly is the characteristic of certain -
questions.explanation: In monocots, the leaf base is often sheathing, partially or wholly covering the stem, as seen in grasses, bananas, and other monocots.

questions.question: What is the function of thin flexible petiole?
options: It helps the plant to climb
It increases the rate of respiration
It allows leaf blade/lamina to flutter in wind there by cooling the leaf and bringing fresh air to leaf surface
It decreases the rate of transpiration
questions.explanation: A thin, flexible petiole allows the lamina to flutter in the wind, which helps cool the leaf and bring fresh air to the surface, facilitating gas exchange.

questions.question: Multifoliate compound leaf (Palmate compound leaf) is found in-
questions.explanation: A multifoliate palmate compound leaf has multiple leaflets emerging from a common point, as seen in Bombax (Silkcotton). Tamarind and Rose → Pinnately compound leaves. Moringa → Bipinnately compound leaves.

questions.question: In a pinnately compound leaf (as seen in Neem) a number of leaflets are present on a common axis, the rachis. The rachis represents the -
questions.explanation: In a pinnately compound leaf (e.g., Neem), multiple leaflets are arranged along the rachis, which is a continuation of the midrib of the leaf.

questions.question: Match Column I with Column II
questions.explanation: Matching explanation: A - IV: Bud in the axil of the leaf → Simple leaf B - III: Bud absent in axil of leaflets → Compound leaf C - II: Spines (modified leaves) → Cacti D - I: Leaves modified to catch insects → Pitcher plant and Venus Fly Trap E - V: Fleshy leaves with stored food → Garlic and Onion

questions.question: Arrangement of leaves on stem or its branches is called
questions.explanation: Phyllotaxy refers to the arrangement of leaves on a stem or branch. It can be alternate, opposite, or whorled.

hi.question: तने या उसकी शाखाओं पर पत्तियों की व्यवस्था कहलाती है:

questions.question: Palmately compound leaf is the one in which the leaflets develop from a common point i.e. at the tip of -
questions.explanation: In a palmately compound leaf, all leaflets arise from a single point at the tip of the petiole, as seen in Silkcotton (Bombax).

questions.question: Leaves are modified into tendrils in -
questions.explanation: In Pea (Pisum sativum), leaves are modified into tendrils to help the plant climb by coiling around a support.

questions.question: Given below is the diagram of a typical leaf. In which of the following all the four parts labelled as A, B, C and D are correctly identified? A B C D (1) Lamina Axillary bud Stipule Leaf base (2) Lamina Stipule Axillary bud Leaf base (3) Lamina Axillary bud Stipule Pedicel (4) Leaflet Axillary bud Stipule Leaf base
questions.explanation: Identification of labeled parts: A - Lamina (broad part of the leaf) B - Axillary bud (present at the axil of the leaf) C - Stipule (small lateral outgrowth at the leaf base) D - Leaf base (the basal part attaching the leaf to the stem) Thus, option (1) Lamina - Axillary bud - Stipule - Leaf base is correct.

questions.question: Study the given figures and identify the kind of phyllotaxy. (i) (ii) (iii)(1) Whorled Opposite Alternate(2) Alternate Opposite Whorled(3) Opposite Alternate Whorled(4) Opposite Whorled Alternate
questions.explanation: [New NCERT Class 11th Page No. 61]

questions.question: Consider the following statement - I. Incision in lamina is always absent in simple leaf II. Petiole is photosynthetic in Australian acacia Mark the correct -
options: Both I and II are correct
questions.explanation: Statement I is incorrect – In a simple leaf, incisions may be present, but they do not reach the midrib. Statement II is correct – In Australian Acacia, the petiole is modified into a phyllode, which performs photosynthesis.

questions.question: Opposite type of phyllotaxy is not present in:
questions.explanation: Opposite phyllotaxy is when two leaves arise at a node opposite to each other. Guava, Calotropis, and Mint show opposite phyllotaxy. Mango exhibits alternate phyllotaxy, not opposite.

questions.question: Leaves become modified into spines in:
questions.explanation: Leaves are modified into spines to reduce water loss and provide protection, commonly seen in xerophytic plants. Opuntia (a cactus) has spines that are modified leaves to minimize transpiration. Onion, Silk Cotton, and Pea do not have leaf spines.

questions.question: Mark the incorrect statement
options: In cymose inflorescence, the main axis terminates in a flower
Flowers are borne on successive internodes on the stems and roots
When a shoot tip transforms into a flower, the flower is always solitary
questions.explanation: The correct answer is:Flowers are borne on successive internodes on the stems and roots.

questions.question: The four whorls of a flower are arranged on the
questions.explanation: The four whorls of a flower (calyx, corolla, androecium, and gynoecium) are arranged on the thalamus, which is the swollen end of the floral axis.

hi.question: पुष्प के चार चक्र व्यवस्थित होते हैं:

questions.question: Radial symmetry is found in flowers of:
questions.explanation: Radial symmetry (actinomorphic flowers) means the flower can be divided into two equal halves along multiple planes. Chilli has radial symmetry (actinomorphic). ✅ Cassia, Gulmohur, and Canna have bilateral symmetry (zygomorphic). ❌

questions.question: Which of the following plant has a superior ovary?
questions.explanation: A superior ovary is present when the ovary is positioned above other floral parts (hypogynous flower). China rose has a superior ovary (hypogynous flower). ✅ Peach and Rose have half-inferior ovaries (perigynous flowers). ❌ Guava has an inferior ovary (epigynous flower). ❌

questions.question: The ray florets of sunflower has
questions.explanation: In sunflower (Helianthus annuus), the ray florets are zygomorphic and sterile, with an inferior ovary where the ovary is fused with the thalamus.

questions.question: Which of the following are not non- essential floral whorl?
questions.explanation: Non-essential floral whorls are those that do not directly participate in reproduction, which are calyx and corolla. Anther is part of the androecium (male reproductive organ), making it essential. ✅ Calyx, Corolla, and Perianth are non-essential. ❌

questions.question: Flower in which all the three remaining floral whorls develop from a point below ovary is called
questions.explanation: A flower in which all three floral whorls (calyx, corolla, and androecium) arise from a point below the ovary is called a hypogynous flower, and the ovary is superior.

If the gynoecium is present in the topmost position of the thalamus, then the flower is referred to as
questions.explanation: If the gynoecium is present at the topmost position of the thalamus, with other floral whorls (calyx, corolla, and androecium) positioned below it, the flower is called hypogynous, and the ovary is superior.

questions.question: Read the given statements. (i) Gynoecium occupies the highest position while the other floral parts are situated below it. (ii) Ovary is superior (iii) Examples are Brassica, Hibiscus, brinjal, etc. Which condition of flowers is being described by the above statements?
questions.explanation: The given statements describe: (i) Gynoecium occupies the highest position while other floral parts are below it. (ii) The ovary is superior. (iii) Examples include Brassica (Mustard), Hibiscus (China rose), and Brinjal, which have hypogynous flowers. This condition is Hypogyny.

questions.question: A flower is
questions.explanation: A flower is: (A) A modified shoot ✅ (Develops from the floral meristem) (B) The reproductive unit in angiosperms ✅ (Responsible for sexual reproduction in flowering plants) (C) Incorrect ❌ (Gymnosperms do not have true flowers, they have cones)

questions.question: Inferior ovary is feature of -
questions.explanation: An inferior ovary is present when the thalamus encloses and fuses with the ovary, characteristic of epigynous flowers. Solanum (Tomato, Brinjal) → Superior ovary (Hypogynous) ❌ Peach → Half-inferior ovary (Perigynous) ❌ Cucumber (Cucurbitaceae) → Inferior ovary (Epigynous) ✅ Mustard → Superior ovary (Hypogynous) ❌

questions.question: The unit of corolla is normally
questions.explanation: The unit of corolla is called a petal, typically non-green and lies inner to sepals. Tepals are found when sepals and petals are indistinguishable, as in monocots.

questions.question: Flower which can be divided into two equal halves in a single longitudinal plane is called
questions.explanation: Since both Zygomorphic and Bilateral symmetry are terms used to describe a flower that can be divided into two equal halves in a single longitudinal plane, the most appropriate choice is "More than one".

questions.question: Match column I with column II and select the correct option from the given codes.
questions.explanation: A. Pedicel - (ii) Stalk of the flower: The stalk of an individual flower is called a pedicel. B. Peduncle - (iv) Inflorescence axis: The main stalk of an inflorescence is known as the peduncle. C. Bract - (i) Reduced leaf: A reduced leaf found at the base of the pedicel is called a bract. D. Petiole - (iii) Stalk of the leaf: The stalk that attaches the leaf blade to the stem is the petiole. Matching these, we get: A-(ii), B-(iv), C-(i), D-(iii). The correct option is A.

questions.question: Refer to the given figures, showing relative position of different floral parts on the thalamus and select the correct option.
questions.explanation: The three floral arrangements are: Hypogynous: Ovary is superior; other floral parts arise below it. Perigynous: Floral parts arise around the ovary, which remains superior. Epigynous: Ovary is inferior; other floral parts arise above it. From the figures: A → Hypogynous B → Hypogynous C → Perigynous D → Epigynous Therefore, the correct combination is Option (4).

questions.question: Perigynous ovary present in -
questions.explanation: Perigynous ovary (half-inferior ovary) is present in: Plum, Peach, and Rose ✅

questions.question: Flower is condensed............
questions.explanation: A flower is a modified and condensed shoot, where the internodes are shortened, and the leaves are modified into floral organs (sepals, petals, stamens, and carpels).

questions.question: The flowers are Zygomorphic in:A. MustardB. GulmoharC. CassiaD. DaturaE. Chilli Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: (C) When a flower can be divided into two equal radial halves in any radial plane passing through the centre, it is said to be actinomorphic, e.g., mustard, datura, chilli. When it can be divided into two similar halves only in one particular vertical plane, it is zygomorphic, e.g., pea, gulmohur, bean, Cassia. [New NCERT class 11th page no. 62]

questions.question: Identify the type of flowers based on the position of calyx, corolla and androecium with respect to the ovary from the given figures (a) and (b) [NEET 2024]
questions.explanation: Position of floral parts on thalamus : (a) Hypogynous, (b) and (c) Perigynous, (d) EpigynousPerigynous: The ovary is partly embedded in the thalamus. The thalamus forms a cup-like structure (hypanthium), and floral parts are attached around the ovary. Hypogynous: The ovary lies above all other floral parts. Sepals, petals, and stamens arise below the ovary. Epigynous: The ovary is completely enclosed by the thalamus, and floral parts appear to arise from above the ovary.

hi.question: दी गई आकृति (a) और (b) से अंडाशय के संबंध में बाह्यदलपुंज, दलपुंज और पुंकेसर की स्थिति के आधार पर फूलों के प्रकार की पहचान कीजिए।
hi.explanation: पुष्पासन (थैलेमस) पर पुष्प भागों की स्थिति: (a) अधोजायांगता (b) और (c) परिजायांगता (d) अधिजायांगता परिजायांगता (पेरिगाइनस): अंडाशय आंशिक रूप से थैलेमस में स्थित होता है। थैलेमस एक कप जैसी संरचना (हाइपेंथियम) बनाता है, और पुष्पीय भाग अंडाशय के चारों ओर जुड़े होते हैं। अधोजायांगता (हाइपोगाइनस) : अंडाशय अन्य सभी पुष्पीय भागों के ऊपर स्थित होता है। बाह्यदल, पंखुड़ियाँ और पुंकेसर अंडाशय के नीचे उत्पन्न होते हैं। अधिजायांगता (एपिगाइनस): अंडाशय पूरी तरह से थैलेमस से घिरा होता है, और पुष्पीय भाग अंडाशय के ऊपर से उत्पन्न होते प्रतीत होते हैं।

questions.question: The statement of assertion is followed by statement of reason, choose the correct option. Assertion (A): Hypogynous flowers have superior ovaries. Reason (R): In hypogynous flowers, Gynoecium occupies the highest position while, petals, sepals and stamens are situated below the ovary.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are True and the Reason (R) is a correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are True but Reason (R) is not a correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is True but the Reason (R) is False.
Assertion (A) is False but the Reason (R) is True.
questions.explanation: Hypogynous flowers have a superior ovary, meaning the gynoecium is at the highest position, and the sepals, petals, and stamens are attached below the ovary (e.g., Mustard, Brinjal). The Reason correctly explains the Assertion, as it describes the relative positioning of floral parts in hypogynous flowers. [New NCERT Class 11 Page No. 79]

questions.question: The statement of assertion is followed by statement of reason, choose the correct option. Assertion (A): Sepals are green, leaf-like and protect the flower in the bud stage.Reason (R): Sepals when united with each other are called polysepalous.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are True and the Reason (R) is a correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are True but Reason (R) is not a correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is True but the Reason (R) is False.
Assertion (A) is False but the Reason (R) is True.
questions.explanation: Sepals are green, leaf-like structures that protect the flower in the bud stage, making Assertion (A) correct. However, when sepals are united, they are called gamosepalous, not polysepalous. Polysepalous refers to free sepals, making Reason (R) incorrect. [New NCERT Class 11 Page No. 79]
